keyword: how much do caddies make at the masters

verifications.claim: Caddies at the Masters can earn over $450,000 for a single win.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'the caddie for the 2026 Masters winner could take home an estimated $450,000'; R2: 'The 2026 Masters winner will make $4.5 million... caddie of the Masters winner earns 10%... could also walk away with six figures'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported by estimates for recent/2026 purse at exactly $450k (10% of $4.5M), 'over' allowed by private contracts or approximations.

verifications.claim: Caddies at the Masters typically receive a weekly fee of $2,000–$4,000.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'weekly wage between $2,000 and $4,000'; identical in R2, R3, R4, R5
verifications.reasoning: Exact range stated directly across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Caddies at the Masters receive 10% of the player's winnings for a victory.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'caddie of the Master's winner will get 10%'; R2: 'caddie of the Masters winner earns 10%'; similar in all others
verifications.reasoning: Consistently and directly stated for winner across all sources.

verifications.claim: Caddies at the Masters receive 7% of the player's winnings for a runner-up finish.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'caddie for the runner up at the Masters will get 7%'; R2: 'caddie of the runner-up gets 7%'; others include as 'top 10' at 7%
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported, with R1 specific to runner-up and others via top-10.

verifications.claim: Caddies at the Masters receive 5% of the player's winnings for making the cut.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'every caddie after that will get 5%'; R2/R3/R4/R5: '5% for making the cut'; R6: '5% for everything else'
verifications.reasoning: Directly and consistently supported for post-cut/making cut finishes.

verifications.claim: For the 2026 purse, a winner's caddie takes home approximately $450,000 from the $4.5 million prize.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '2026 Masters winner will make $4.5 million from a $22.5 million purse'; R5: 'Masters purse totals $22.5 million... winner will take home $4.5 million... caddie... estimated $450,000'
verifications.reasoning: Exact purse, winner prize, and 10% caddie calculation directly stated.

verifications.claim: Runner-up caddie pay at the Masters is ~7% of winnings (e.g., ~$226,800).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3/R4/R5: 'Justin Rose, the runner up, won $2.268 million; his caddie... received around $226,800' and '7% for a top 10 finish'; R2 states 7% for runner-up and cites $2.268 million runner-up purse
verifications.reasoning: Sources state 7% for runner-up/top-10 and provide the exact example amount for a named runner-up, faithfully represented despite minor internal math discrepancy.

verifications.claim: Top-10 finish caddie pay at the Masters is ~5%–7% of winnings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3/R4/R5/R6: '7% for a top 10 finish'; R1: 'runner up... 7%... every caddie after that... 5%'
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify 7% for top-10 (or runner-up within top-10) and 5% for others making cut, directly supporting the range.

verifications.claim: For missed cut, caddies at the Masters generally only receive their weekly base fee ($2,000–$4,000).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'if your player doesn't make the cut, there is no other source of money other than the weekly fee'; identical in all others with $2,000–$4,000 range
verifications.reasoning: Directly and unanimously stated across sources.

verifications.claim: Caddies at the Masters are responsible for their own travel, lodging, and food.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'required to pay their own travel to Georgia, along with hotel and food'; identical phrasing in R2–R5; R6: 'caddies have to pay for all of their own expenses, airfare, hotel, rental car, food'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated in exact terms across all sources.

verifications.claim: Caddies at the Masters' travel, lodging, and food expenses are covered by the weekly wage.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The weekly wage helps caddies recoup financially because they're required to pay their own travel... hotel and food'; similar in others
verifications.reasoning: Directly implied and stated that weekly wage is provided to cover/recoup those self-paid expenses.

verifications.claim: Caddies at Augusta National have their own locker room.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'We had our own locker room'; R2 quotes: 'We had our own locker room'
verifications.reasoning: Direct quote from caddie in both sources.

verifications.claim: Caddies at Augusta National receive premium meals.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'They feed us just wonderful food — the best food I've ever had really'; R2 quotes same
verifications.reasoning: 'Wonderful... best food' directly supports 'premium meals' description.
